papers.findings: Discussion condition wins 75.6% of 250 paired monologues; Craft/Clarity +0.440, Social Response +0.422; occasional aggression increase.
papers.what_it_gives: Characters must remember what audiences and other characters thought of them, not just prior scripts. Social memory as conditioning signal.

papers.findings: Rank 1 (tied) all three languages; agentic variants Exp09/Exp10 not superior to pipeline despite higher tool budgets.
papers.what_it_gives: Planner to Best-of-N Writer to Reflector to Judge over a 98-joke mechanism corpus. Simple generator + good selection beats writers-room sprawl. Repo in data/github/ragthoven.

papers.findings: Mechanism mastery (incongruity, conciseness, escalation, absurdity) beats scale; specialists reach parity with far larger systems; cross-judge tau 0.889.
papers.what_it_gives: GTVH-grounded pairwise judging (mechanism + delivery + failure tags) aggregated by Adaptive Swiss + Bradley-Terry. Head-to-head mechanism comparison per character.

papers.authors: Narad, Suresh, Chen, Dysart-Bricken, Mankoff, Nowak, Zhang, Jain
papers.findings: STEM reasoning transfers to humor comprehension; autograder 92% vs human experts; test-time scaling mixed.
papers.note: Dataset cartoons are copyrighted (New Yorker/Cartoonstock). Paper shelved; source images NOT mirrored.
papers.what_it_gives: ~300 cartoon-caption pairs with 1-3 objective element rubrics. The critic must explain the mechanism, not score out of ten.

papers.findings: Field shift to alignment + evidence-grounded reasoning + controlled generation; barriers: shortcut evals, thin cultural coverage, weak grounding, safety/ownership gaps.
papers.what_it_gives: StaVT vs SeqVN taxonomy. Physical performance, faces, timing, visual contradiction need independent representation, not text-to-speech.

papers.findings: Two experiments support: playful turn + motive-consistency yields mirth; failed jokes lowest on motive-consistency.
papers.what_it_gives: Scene framing rule: same shocking line lands or offends depending on relationship, expectation, and prior emotional state.
